title: One hour here (Avot 4:17)
hookLine: an hour between one thing and the next: one hour of return and good deeds here outweighs all the life of the world to come
tomorrow: your friend is crying right now. is right now the time to talk?

cards: The show's over. The set's coming down. There's an hour before the party, and it could go anywhere: scrolling, napping, replaying the night.
If this world is just the hallway, does any hour here count? The very next saying in Avot answers, and it answers in a way that sounds almost upside down.

teach.h: ONE HOUR HERE OUTWEIGHS ALL THERE.
teach.b: Here it is, in plain words. Better one hour of return and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come. And better one hour of calm in the world to come than all the life of this world.
Read the first half again. One hour here outweighs everything there. Why?

teach.h: HERE IS WHERE YOU CAN STILL ACT.
teach.b: Because in this picture, the corridor is the only place where you can still act. Teshuvah, return, turning back from a wrong, and good deeds, happen here. The banquet hall is for rest, not for doing.
So the hallway isn't a waste of time. It's the only time there is for doing. Then the second half balances it.

teach.h: ONE HOUR OF CALM THERE, TOO.
teach.b: One hour of calm there outweighs all of life here.
Both are true at once, and the saying doesn't make you choose.
That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: Avot says one hour of doing good here is worth more than all of heaven, and one hour of heaven's calm is worth more than all of here.
So what do you do with one free hour this week? Not a whole new life. One hour.
The text you've been meaning to send. The apology you've been rehearsing. The help nobody asked for.

how: Jewish tradition treats teshuvah, return, as open every day, and many Jews use the month before Rosh Hashanah and the days up to Yom Kippur to make apologies and set things right with others.

o: an hour of prayer each day is required by Jewish law
one hour of doing good here outweighs all of heaven
heaven lasts only one hour for every good deed done

games.q: the two halves — tap the pairs.
p: one hour of return and good deeds here
better than all life in the world to come
one hour of calm in the world to come
better than all the life of this world
return: turning back from a wrong

s: Avot says this world is just a waiting room that doesn't count
one hour of return and good deeds here outweighs all the life of the world to come.
the saying has two halves that weigh in opposite directions
doing good here outweighs there; calm there outweighs all of here. both are true at once.
Avot says return can only happen once a year, on Yom Kippur
the saying speaks of any hour of return and good deeds in this world.

games.q: your grandmother's in a care home across town. you have a free hour on Sunday and a long list of things you could do with it. what does today's saying weigh?
o: one hour of a good deed here is worth more than it looks; visit her.
save the visit for a long weekend, when you can give her a whole day.
rest; one hour of calm is worth more than everything else anyway.
games.why: one hour here outweighs all of there, because here is where you can still act. the calm the saying praises belongs to the world to come.

practice: Make a small plan for one hour this week. First, the wish: one act of return or one good deed you'd use the hour for. Next, the obstacle that usually eats that hour.
Then the plan: when the obstacle shows up, what you'll do instead.

wordCard.voice: One hour here. Avot: one hour of return and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the world to come.

orig.note: Hebrew: one hour, the measure both halves of the saying use.

carryVoice: For the road: one hour here, the only place for doing. Forty-one of sixty, and the hour is yours.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 4:17 (better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come)
